blindFindings.where: s4 'an audacious tiger' in West African oral tales; repeated 'the tale of the tiger'
blindFindings.finding: Tigers are not native to Africa (Asian species). A West African tale would feature a leopard. Presented as traditional West African story content.

blindFindings.where: s7 'Pewee is reading a Liberian folktale ... The cunning fox'
blindFindings.finding: Foxes do not occur in Liberia; the fox trickster is a European (Reynard) convention. Liberian trickster tales typically feature Spider, and also tortoise/turtle and other local animals. Needs verification.
West African trickster is the hare; rabbits are not native there. 'Rabbit' appears in some Liberian English retellings so this is minor.
European imagery presented as context; and 'quaint', 'spartan', 'ballyhoo', 'pomp' are culturally Western, low-frequency words.

Context-clue questions give no actual sentence to read; the 'context' (no decorations, cobblestones, decorations and dances) appears only inside the answers. Learners cannot use context clues that are not provided; the method is circular.
All six items have the answer text as the studentPrompt and an empty answerKey; there is no question for learners to answer. Assessment is broken.
No guided practice, independent practice, assessment, exit ticket or closing; body ends at Error Analysis. Section 5 missing. takeawaySummary consists only of questions, not takeaways.

blindFindings.where: s8 Try this 'With fervor akin to a hunted deer'
blindFindings.finding: Faulty model sentence: a hunted deer suggests fear/flight, not fervor; models poor usage and misleads the inference.
'"clear" is a synonym for "unclouded"' but 'unclouded' is not in the example sentence; confusing example.
False etymology (infer < Latin inferre, 'bring in'); 'fuse' association is misleading.

blindFindings.where: s7 step 2 'If you're outwitted, you're puzzled or unsure'
blindFindings.finding: Overgeneralisation; outwitted means beaten by cleverness, not necessarily confused. The real clue is 'unsure of what had just happened'.
Ornate adult prose ('tapestry', 'vivid tableau', 'constellation of meanings') far above G7 reading level; sections carry author word-count headings ('(300+ words)').
Monrovia sits on a low coastal plain/Cape Mesurado; 'hills surrounding' is loose but minor.
Title promises West African texts but no actual West African text or excerpt is read; all sentences are invented.
